rows: $f=1/T$; $v=2\pi r/T=2\pi rf$. Uniform circle: $r$ radius (m), $T$ period (s), $f$ frequency (Hz), $v$ speed (m/s).
$\theta=s/r$ in radians for arc length $s$. Uniform angular speed $\omega=2\pi/T$ (rad/s); $v=r\omega$ and $a_r=r\omega^2$. A full turn is $2\pi$ radians.
$\Delta\mathbf v=\mathbf v_2-\mathbf v_1$; $\overline{\mathbf a}=\Delta\mathbf v/\Delta t$. Subtract vectors, not speeds. A finite average need not equal an instantaneous acceleration.
$a_r=v^2/r=4\pi^2r/T^2$, inward. Velocity is tangent. For uniform speed, acceleration is entirely radial; if speed varies, a tangential component also exists.
$\sum F_{\rm inward}=mv^2/r$ for the radial component of Newton’s second law. Draw real interactions only. “Centripetal” names the inward resultant, not an extra force.
Flat horizontal circle, weight/contact only vertically: $N=mg$. Sticking requires $mv^2/r\leq\mu_sN$; hence $v_{\max}=\sqrt{\mu_sgr}$. $\mu_s$ is a dimensionless friction coefficient.
String length $L$, angle $\theta$ to vertical: $r=L\sin\theta$; $S\cos\theta=mg$; $S\sin\theta=mv^2/r$. Thus $v^2=rg\tan\theta$ for $0<\theta<90^\circ$. $S$ is tension.
Top: $S+mg=mv_t^2/r$. Bottom: $S-mg=mv_b^2/r$. Inward positive at each. A cord needs $S\geq0$; top condition $v_t\geq\sqrt{gr}$ is local, not a complete launch criterion.
An unattached contact needs $N\geq0$; a cord cannot push. Negative required support means the assumed constrained path fails. Do not take its absolute value.
$F=GMm/r^2$; $g(r)=GM/r^2=\mu/r^2$; $\mu=GM$. Attractive pair forces have equal magnitudes on different recipients. Exact for point masses or non-overlapping spherical mass distributions.
$r=R+h$: centre distance, source radius and altitude. $G\approx6.67430\times10^{-11}$ N m²/kg²; $\mu$ in m³/s²; $g$ in m/s² or N/kg. Weight $mg$ differs from a support reading.
$v=\sqrt{\mu/r}$; $T=2\pi\sqrt{r^3/\mu}$. Exterior circular path, dominant spherical source treated as fixed, gravity only. Velocity must be tangential. Satellite mass cancels.
$k=r/r_0$, $q=\mu/\mu_0$: $v/v_0=\sqrt{q/k}$; $T/T_0=\sqrt{k^3/q}$; $g/g_0=q/k^2$. Each point is a separate scenario, not time evolution.
